mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-31.6 to -12.1). This momentum reflects accumulating pent-up demand release and will continue to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as consumers progressively resume shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite the four-week monotonic uptrend persisting through the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved by roughly 6-9 points per week as Victoria eases Stage 4 restrictions. If WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points week-on-week, it signals an official reopening step that drives commuter-linked retail visits upward within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -42.4 to -25.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the 2 weeks following a WORKPLACES week-on-week jump greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: Joint sustained improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates restored commuting patterns that combine with habitual shopping stops, producing an amplified rise in RETAIL_REC beyond what either series would predict alone over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -46.4 to -26.1 while WORKPLACES improved from -42.4 to -25.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over next 4 weeks is no greater than the sum of growth rates implied by TRANSIT and WORKPLACES individually, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 5.1 to 1.4, indicating reduced time spent at home under easing restrictions. This behavioral shift toward leaving home predicts a continued rise in RETAIL_REC as residents redirect freed time to retail and recreation visits.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 5.1 to 1.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 2 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL continues its downward trend below 1.4.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has spiked to 65.0 as Melbourne enters spring (September), reflecting a seasonal substitution where residents prioritize outdoor recreation over indoor retail visits, which will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 65.0 in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a PARKS reading above 60, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Victoria's roadmap ties retail reopening to sustained low case numbers and specific restriction-easing dates. If TRANSIT crosses above -30 (indicating a step-change easing threshold reached), it signals a policy-triggered retail reopening phase that lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -30 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -26.1 at t-0w, crossing above -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after TRANSIT first exceeds -30, indicating the threshold is not policy-linked to retail reopening.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has narrowed from -24.4 to -9.4, showing growing comfort with in-person essential shopping. This rebuilding of general shopping confidence is a leading behavioral indicator that will extend to non-essential retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -24.4 to -9.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth decouples from GROCERY_PHARM improvement, i.e., GROCERY_PHARM keeps improving while RETAIL_REC stalls or declines over the next 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week increments in RETAIL_REC are shrinking (8.5, 7.1, 3.9 points), indicating decelerating momentum. This deceleration, combined with similarly decelerating WORKPLACES gains, predicts a plateau or reversal in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as the initial reopening surge exhausts itself.
candidate_trigger: weekly RETAIL_REC increment falls below 4 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gains shrank from 8.5 to 7.1 to 3.9 points across the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds the last 28 days despite two consecutive weeks of sub-4-point gains in both RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES.
